subject: CareCura — scope for subprocessor evidence and on-demand auditor access
messages:
From: Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@carecura.com>
To: logan_wright@redwood.com
Cc: legal@carecura.com
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: DPIA support + subprocessor access exceptions (CareCura)
Attachments: CareCura_DPIA_questionnaire_v2.pdf (application/pdf)

Hi Logan,

Thanks for taking this on. As part of our DPIA and procurement diligence I need evidence around a couple of specific items before the next security review on July 6: 

- Art. 30 processing register excerpt that shows which subprocessors process CareCura production data.
- Access logs or sampled session records for two subprocessors (CloudOpsX and MetricsStream) for Apr–May 2027 — we specifically need any records of privileged access or emergency break-glass sessions.
- Clarification on cross-border transfer mechanisms used for those subprocessors (SCCs, BCRs, or EU-hosted replicas).
- Confirmation of whether you can provide a time-limited auditor access path or on-site remote review for our external auditor under NDA — and if any exceptions exist where a subprocessor had ad-hoc privileged access (we need an annotated exception report if so).

We attached our standard questionnaire (CareCura_DPIA_questionnaire_v2.pdf). Can you confirm what you can hand over as ISO artifacts and an estimated timeline?

Elena Martinez
Head of Privacy, CareCura
elena.martinez@carecura.com

--
CareCura Legal (cc) — please flag any contractual items that would block on-demand access or sampling of logs.

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@carecura.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: DPIA support + subprocessor access exceptions (CareCura)
Attachments: initial-evidence-plan.txt (text/plain)

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front then a proposed plan: 

1) Art. 30: we can provide an export of the processing register and the DPA subprocessor appendix (redacted contact emails).
2) Logs: we can produce sampled access logs for the named subprocessors for Apr–May 2027. We will redact end-user PII fields but retain timestamps, actor IDs, and justification tags.
3) Transfers: CloudOpsX operates in a US region with SCCs in place; MetricsStream is EU-hosted for production telemetry with SCCs as fallback — I will ask Kimberly to attach the transfer diagram and current legal basis summary.
4) Auditor access: we support two modes — a secure remote review (encrypted, time-limited share of logs + live read-only console session) or a supervised on-site remote session with our engineer. Both require an executed NDA + a scope-of-review doc.

Proposed timeline:
- Today: acknowledge and confirm scope (this thread).
- 48–72 hours: delivery of processing register export + transfer summary + evidence plan (we'll include sampling methodology).
- 5 business days: sampled logs and annotated exception report (if exceptions exist).

Can we schedule a 30-minute sync tomorrow to confirm the sampling windows and redaction requirements? I included Marissa (privacy) and Kimberly (security) to handle the artifacts.

Regards,
Logan Wright
Manager, Customer Privacy — Redwood Inference
logan_wright@redwood.com
+1 415 555 0198

--
Attachment: initial-evidence-plan.txt outlines sampling approach, redaction rules, and temporary auditor access checklist.

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@carecura.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 11:30:00 -0400
Subject: Re: DPIA support + subprocessor access exceptions (CareCura)
Attachments: exception-playbook.pdf (application/pdf)

Hi Elena / Logan — quick technical clarifications from the security side: 

- Retention / format: logs are stored for 90 days in compressed JSONL. We can export to CSV if preferred for your reviewer. The export will include actor_id, session_start, session_end, resource_affected, action, and support_notes. PII columns will be redacted per our standard redaction policy.
- CloudOpsX exceptional access: there was one incident on 2027-05-03 where CloudOpsX performed emergency troubleshooting resulting in elevated console access for ~40 minutes. We will produce an "annotated exception" that includes why access was granted, who approved it, and what artifacts were accessed. We do not consider this a recurring pattern but will include the playbook and escalation notes.
- Auditor access mode: for an external auditor we prefer a supervised remote session (time-limited read-only console) plus a pre-signed bundle (hashed and time-limited). We will not provide write or shell-level access. If your audit team insists on physical on-site access, we'll need a DSAR / POA and to scope out the environment.

I'll turn around the annotated exception and the transfer diagram by EOD tomorrow. Attaching our internal exception playbook for reference.

Kimberly Park
Senior Security Engineer — Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

--
Attachment: exception-playbook.pdf (redacted operational playbook for emergency access).

From: Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@carecura.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@carecura.com
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 15:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: DPIA support + subprocessor access exceptions (CareCura)

Logan / Kimberly / Marissa — thank you, that plan works. A couple quick follow-ups: 

- Please supply the Art. 30 excerpt and the transfer diagram as separate files. We will need the annotated exception log and the sampling CSV no later than EOD Mon (2027-06-28) to make our scheduler for the review.
- For auditor access, CareCura prefers the supervised remote session + hashed bundle. We will circulate an NDA and scope-of-review doc (our external auditor requires that in DocuSign). Please confirm whether you can accept a limited DocuSign NDA (I will send the link).
- Contract note: our legal team will propose a short redline to the DPA clarifying the on-demand auditor process and maximum data scope. I have cc'd legal.

Once we have the artifacts I'd like to schedule the supervised review the week of July 5. Thanks again for the quick turnaround.

Best,
Elena Martinez
Head of Privacy — CareCura

--
CareCura Legal: we'll wait for your redline and notify if additional contractual controls are required.
